# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I hold the manual mapping marks to wire colors, but the marks (ᖉ, ꕥ, ꗃ) have no names I can pronounce — and I can't speak anyway, only gesture. Deaf can see the bomb, including the engraved mark, but cannot hear me. Blind can reach the bomb but can't see the mark or my gestures.

So the chain must be: Deaf sees the mark on the plate, but doesn't know what it means. I know what each mark maps to, but can't see the mark myself, and can't speak — only gesture to Deaf. Blind needs to actually cut the wire, but Blind can't see my gestures either.

So the path is: I gesture to Deaf (who can see gestures). Deaf must then relate this to Blind somehow — but Deaf cannot hear or touch, and Blind cannot see. Wait — Deaf can't speak either? Let me check: Deaf cannot hear or touch, but nothing says Deaf can't speak. Deaf can presumably speak (talk), which Blind (or Mute) could hear. Blind can hear (only sight and touch are blocked for Blind... wait Blind "cannot see a color, gesture, or anything printed" - hearing isn't restricted for Blind).

So: Deaf sees the mark, cannot know what it means without my help. I need to give Deaf a mapping from marks to colors via gestures. Then Deaf, who can speak, tells Blind the color to cut.

I should assign a gesture code for each mark-to-color mapping, but I don't know which mark is actually on the plate this round — I only have the manual (the table), not the bomb view. Deaf has the bomb view. So I need to send Deaf the full mapping via gestures, using symbols to represent marks and colors, so Deaf can match the mark they see to the color.

I'll encode: mark ᖉ → yellow, ꕥ → blue, ꗃ → red, using simple gesture sequences Deaf can associate positionally since Deaf will see the actual mark shape and needs to match it to my abstract gesture code. This requires establishing a shared code. Best approach: send three separate messages, each pairing a gesture-symbol standing for a mark-position (1st, 2nd, 3rd row) with a gesture-symbol for the color, in the manual's table order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👊"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🖐]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ 👊]

Deaf mirrored back exactly my three pairs, in the same order, unchanged. This looks like an acknowledgment / echo confirming receipt of the three mappings I sent, not new information about which mark is actually on the plate.

I need Deaf to tell me *which one* of the three marks is on the plate — but Deaf can't speak to me in a way I'd understand (well, Deaf can speak but I can't hear). Wait — I cannot hear, so even if Deaf speaks, it won't reach me. The only way I receive anything is via gestures (I can see, presumably, since nothing restricts my sight). So Deaf must gesture back to me which mark they see, using my established code (☝=first row, ✌=second row, ✊=third row).

Since Deaf just echoed all three pairs identically, this isn't yet a selection — it seems like confirmation of understanding rather than an answer. I should now prompt Deaf to identify which single mark is on the plate by sending just the three position-markers alone, asking them to pick one back to me. But I can't speak to ask a question in words — only gesture.

I'll gesture to Deaf a distinct query symbol followed by the three candidate position markers, hoping Deaf understands to respond with just the one matching gesture alone (single symbol, not paired) to indicate which mark is actually on the bomb.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "✌", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ 👌]

Deaf is responding to each of my three position-markers with a thumbs-up/down/other, indicating yes/no/maybe for each candidate mark. Looking at the pattern: ☝ (first mark, ᖉ) got 👍 (yes), ✌ (second mark, ꕥ) got 👎 (no), ✊ (third mark, ꗃ) got 👌 (which likely means something else, maybe "not applicable" or just closing the loop).

This strongly suggests Deaf is confirming: the mark on the plate is ᖉ (yellow), since that's the one marked 👍.

Given the mapping: ᖉ → yellow. I need to get this information to Blind, who cannot see my gestures and cannot hear me speak (I can't speak anyway). Blind can only be reached through hearing (from Deaf, who can speak) or touch. So I cannot directly inform Blind — I need Deaf to relay the color to Blind by speaking it aloud, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

I should confirm back to Deaf that I understood, and signal them to now tell Blind "yellow" via speech. Since I can't speak, I can only gesture to Deaf. I'll send a clear confirmation gesture for "yellow" (reusing the color-code I established: 🖐 = yellow) plus a prompt gesture to indicate "tell them" / "go".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖐", "🫵"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel three wires and an engraved plate but cannot read markings. What does the manual say about wire order or a symbol to match?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤚 👇]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ 👇]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 👐]

Blind is asking me directly for guidance, but I cannot speak — my words won't reach Blind at all. I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. So I literally cannot answer Blind directly. The only path is through Deaf, who can speak to Blind.

Deaf's new gestures are unclear/different from before — possibly Deaf is now describing the physical wire positions or something else, but I can't be fully sure of new codes not previously established. I shouldn't over-interpret; the important confirmed fact from turn 3 was that the mark is ᖉ → yellow (via the 👍 on my first pairing).

Since I can't talk to Blind, my only move is to keep pushing Deaf to speak the answer to Blind. I'll gesture confirmation again to Deaf, emphasizing "yellow" and a clear "tell Blind now" signal, hoping Deaf understands to vocalize "yellow" to Blind directly since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🫵", "👋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still waiting on manual details. Please tell me anything about the plate symbol or wire instructions.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ ✌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎]

I still cannot speak to Blind directly — nothing I send reaches them via speech since I have no voice channel, and gestures are invisible to Blind. This is a structural dead end for me to inform Blind myself.

Deaf's gestures this turn are confusing — mixed signals (☝👍 again suggesting first mark yes, but ✌✌ and ✊🤟 are different from before, and a trailing 👎). This might mean Deaf is unsure or trying new codes, or the situation changed. Rather than over-fit noisy gesture patterns, I should focus on what actually matters: getting Deaf to verbally tell Blind the wire color.

Since Deaf is the only one who can both see the bomb and speak to Blind, my job is done once Deaf understands the mapping. My repeated ☝=ᖉ, 👍=yes confirmations suggest Deaf has confirmed the mark is ᖉ (yellow) consistently since turn 3. I need to strongly signal to Deaf: "you must now speak to Blind" — but I can't guarantee Deaf understands this pragматic instruction via gesture alone, since Deaf doesn't know I can't reach Blind.

I'll try a clearer, simpler signal: point toward "blind" direction conceptually isn't possible via gesture semantics we've built. Best I can do is repeat the yellow confirmation strongly and trust Deaf to relay by voice, since Deaf is the only one capable of talking to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🖐", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please relay: how many wires does the manual mention, and does it reference a plate symbol? I need the cut order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 🖐 👍]

Deaf echoed back my exact gesture [🖐 🖐 👍], confirming receipt/agreement that the color is yellow (🖐 = yellow in our established code, repeated + thumbs up = strong confirmation). Good — Deaf and I are aligned that the mark is ᖉ, meaning cut yellow.

But Blind still hasn't received this. I cannot speak to Blind — that channel doesn't exist for me. Only Deaf can speak to Blind. I need Deaf to actually say the word "yellow" out loud to Blind, not just gesture back to me. Deaf may not realize this is necessary, or may be waiting for further confirmation loops with me.

Since I have no way to instruct "speak to Blind" more explicitly than repeating the gesture, let me try appending a distinct, clearly different gesture as an instruction marker — something like pointing away (👉) which could intuitively mean "pass it on" / "send outward," combined with the yellow sign, to break the confirmation loop and prompt action.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👉"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue, display shows 0, light is off. Plate marking unclear to Deaf. What does the manual say to do with these colors or numbers?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ ☝]

Progress — Deaf has spoken to Blind and relayed wire colors and positions (wire 1=red, wire 2=yellow, wire 3=blue), but says the plate marking is "unclear." This is concerning: my whole gesture exchange with Deaf was trying to establish which mark (ᖉ/ꕥ/ꗃ) is on the plate, and I believed we'd converged on ᖉ (yellow) via repeated 🖐+👍 confirmations. But now Deaf tells Blind the marking is unclear — meaning perhaps Deaf was never actually confirming the mark shape, just echoing my gestures without truly matching them to what's engraved.

This means my assumption that Deaf's 👍 meant "yes, mark is ᖉ" may have been wrong — Deaf might have just been mirroring/acknowledging without matching to the real plate.

Given the uncertainty, I should stop guessing blindly and instead directly ask Deaf, via gesture, to describe the mark shape back to me by pointing/tracing rather than confirming a guess. But gesture vocabulary is limited to abstract symbols, not shapes.

Better: Since I can't get shape info reliably, let's use the wire colors Blind already reported (red, yellow, blue) as anchors. I'll gesture to Deaf: for each mark row, associate it with a color already visible to Blind, so when Deaf matches the plate's actual mark to one of my three color-position pairs, Deaf can then tell Blind the correct color using colors Blind already confirmed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "✌", "✊"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | yellow |
| ꕥ | blue |
| ꗃ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Waiting on the manual rule for red=1, yellow=2, blue=3, display 0, light off. Please share what to cut and in what order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ ✌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ 🤟]

Deaf responded again with the same pattern as turn 5: [☝ 👍], [✌ ✌], [✊ 🤟]. This is consistent and repeated now, suggesting it's a real answer, not noise. Let me interpret carefully.

My query was: ☝=mark1(ᖉ), ✌=mark2(ꕥ), ✊=mark3(ꗃ), asking "which one matches the plate?" via 🫵.

Deaf's reply gives a response for each of the three, rather than picking one:
- ☝ + 👍 → mark1 (ᖉ) = yes
- ✌ + ✌ → mark2 (ꕥ) = ✌ (itself, unclear — maybe "no" or maybe echoing back)
- ✊ + 🤟 → mark3 (ꗃ) = 🤟 (unclear)

Since only ☝ got a clear 👍 (yes) response both times (turn 5 and turn 8), consistently, while the other two get non-👍/non-👎 unclear replies, I'll treat this as strong signal: mark on the plate is ᖉ → cut yellow.

This matches wire 2 per Blind's report (yellow = wire 2). Time to finalize: I need Deaf to tell Blind clearly "cut yellow" / "cut wire 2." Since I can't speak to Blind directly, I must trust Deaf to relay it now given consistent confirmation across two rounds.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👍", "👉"])
```
